lines.say: Why do your muscles get so big during a workout, then shrink back?
That's the pump. Here's what's happening.
Every rep squeezes the veins inside your muscle.
Blood keeps rushing in, but it can't get out as fast.
Your hard working cells also fill up with waste products.
Those pull water in, so the cells swell up like balloons.
When you rest, the blood drains away and the pump fades.
Does the pump itself build muscle? Scientists are still debating it.
But it's a sign your muscle just did a lot of work.
Next time: why do your knees crack?
